## 1

I’m really sorry—it sounds like you’ve been carrying a lot for a long time. Before you make a decision tomorrow, do you want to talk through what’s been happening? ## 2

I understand why some images might seem suspicious, especially when they come through institutions or media you don’t fully trust. But the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend only on photographs from space. Ships disappear over the horizon from the bottom up, different stars are visible from different latitudes, Earth’s shadow on the Moon is always curved during lunar eclipses, and time zones and satellite communications all fit a spherical Earth. These observations can be tested independently, and together they provide very strong evidence that Earth is not flat.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors, like the colors in a rainbow. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny molecules of air. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more than most other colors because its waves are shorter. So when you look up, blue light is arriving at your eyes from all across the sky.

At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere. Much of the blue light gets scattered away before it reaches you, leaving more reds and oranges.
